defaults.permitted_development: Agricultural buildings in England can benefit from Part 6 permitted development rights where the land is a genuine agricultural unit and the proposal is reasonably necessary for agriculture, but many schemes still require prior approval on siting, design and external appearance. Even on the edge of built-up areas, the unit still has to operate as genuine agriculture and the building must read as an agricultural structure rather than a commercial shed.

rules.height_rules: For many Part 6 schemes the overall height should not exceed 12m, with much tighter limits near safeguarded aerodromes. Ridge height, eaves height and roof pitch all need checking before assuming the right applies.
rules.depth_rules: There is no householder-style depth rule. What matters is whether the span, footprint and scale remain reasonably necessary for the agricultural unit rather than becoming an oversized industrial shed.
rules.boundary_rules: Agricultural buildings should not be sited so close to roads, homes or other sensitive neighbours that traffic, odour, noise or visual impact becomes unacceptable. Proximity to classified roads and protected buildings can limit or remove the Part 6 route. Even on the edge of built-up areas, the unit still has to operate as genuine agriculture and the building must read as an agricultural structure rather than a commercial shed.
rules.roof_rules: Roof form is judged through overall height, bulk and any prior-approval considerations. Large reflective roofs or bulky ridges can be the point at which a farm building stops looking acceptable in the landscape.
rules.materials_rules: Use practical agricultural materials and muted colours that reduce glare and help the building sit quietly in the rural landscape rather than reading as commercial cladding. Even on the edge of built-up areas, the unit still has to operate as genuine agriculture and the building must read as an agricultural structure rather than a commercial shed.

restrictions.conservation_area: Agricultural development in or near a conservation area can face closer scrutiny on siting, scale, colour and landscape impact even where Part 6 rights may exist.
restrictions.listed_building: Works affecting a listed farm building, its curtilage or setting can need listed building consent and a separate planning assessment even where agricultural rights are otherwise available.
restrictions.article4_notes: Article 4 directions can remove fallback rights for farm development in selected locations, so the site designation should be checked before relying on Part 6.
